'''Italian ice''', also known as '''water ice''', is a frozen dessert made from either concentrated syrup flavoring or fruit purees.

== Ingredients ==
*2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
*1 cups light [[Cookbook:Corn Syrup|corn syrup]]
*½ cup white [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*⅔ cup [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]] juice

== Procedure ==
#In heavy, medium-sized [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], stir together water, corn syrup, and sugar.
#Heat to [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiling]] over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to low and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]], uncovered, 5 minutes.
#Remove from heat; cool for 30 minutes. Stir in lemon juice.
#Pour mixture into a 9 inch square baking pan. Cover surface with [[Cookbook:Plastic Wrap|plastic wrap]]. 
#Freeze 3–4 hours, or until frozen but still soft in center.
#Spoon into [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]] container; cover. Blend on high speed until mixture becomes white and creamy.
#Turn back into the pan. Cover with plastic wrap. Freeze mixture about 3 hours or until firm.

steps.text: In heavy, medium-sized saucepan, stir together water, corn syrup, and sugar.
Heat to boiling over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to low and simmer, uncovered, 5 minutes.
Remove from heat; cool for 30 minutes. Stir in lemon juice.
Pour mixture into a 9 inch square baking pan. Cover surface with plastic wrap.
Freeze 3–4 hours, or until frozen but still soft in center.
Spoon into blender container; cover. Blend on high speed until mixture becomes white and creamy.
Turn back into the pan. Cover with plastic wrap. Freeze mixture about 3 hours or until firm.
